title: Graded, revise or human review
statement: Let a written-answer marker return graded, revise or human review, sending ambiguity, conflicting evidence, rubric gaps and low confidence to a person instead of forcing a verdict.
example: One Grade 5 grader sends an answer to a person whenever the provider's confidence falls below 0.85.
detail: A Grade 5 course's grader for written answers grounds its evaluation in supplied passage evidence and a versioned rubric, runs deterministic grounding guards before the model call, records the rubric and prompt versions, and returns one of three states: graded, revise or human review. It requires a person for ambiguity, conflicting evidence, a rubric that does not cover the answer, or provider confidence below 0.85. An AP teaching contract likewise records a low-confidence written answer without mastery or points and routes it to a person.
against: The grader's handover says its presence does not certify all 550 items or prove production scale or delivery (`grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/adversarial-course-council/initiatives/05-g5-xp-scoring-progression-and-qti-runtime/HANDOVER.md`, line 52). Another build on record goes further and lets a model's confident reading of a student's words choose a hint or move on, but never give a grade (keep-the-words-a-hint-not-a-grade).

evidence.quote: - grounds evaluation in supplied passage evidence and a versioned rubric; - requires human review for ambiguity, conflicting evidence, rubric insufficiency, or provider confidence below 0.85; - uses deterministic grounding guards before the model call; - records rubric/prompt versions and returns graded/revise/human-review states.
A low-confidence constructed response is recorded without mastery or XP and routed to human review.
